# Agent Note: Session cost figure and the billed-usage projection

Status: implemented

English | [中文](2026-08-29-composer-session-cost.zh.md)

## Problem

The peak/valley status row named the billing window but never what the session costs. DeepSeek's official schedule halves every rate off-peak, and requests land in different windows at different Beijing times, so a session total needs per-request usage paired with the window each request started in. The client had neither: `tokenUsage` folds whole-log totals without time, and the chat window only carries the paged suffix's nodes. The cost also had to stay an opt-in figure (independent of the peak/valley switch), reprice instantly when the user edits prices, and never show a fabricated number for a session whose usage is unknown.

## Decision

**Host fold: `billedUsage`.** Token-meter gains a fourth projection unit. The fold splits every usage sample into two price-independent bucket sets — peak and off-peak — using the same official schedule as the row (`billing-window.ts`, Beijing UTC+8, weekday 09:00–12:00 ∪ 14:00–18:00). Each sample bills at the window of its step's `step/start` instant, so a request straddling a boundary prices at the instant it began; a sample without a matching step start (a usage chunk in a truncated log) falls back to its own event time. Buckets are `{missInputTokens, cacheReadTokens, outputTokens}` with cache writes folded into the miss side, mirroring the disjoint billing buckets the stats line already documents. Samples follow the `tokenUsage` replace rule (a finalized `assistant/message` usage replaces the same step's earlier chunk), so the state stays O(1) and the wire view is eight integers — the projection carriers ship whole views, which a per-step ledger would have made quadratic.

**Client pricing: `price-calculator.ts`.** A pure module owns the official price table — each period's own published columns, idle and peak, for every bucket (`deepseek-v4-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`) — model resolution (user-edited entry → official column, case-insensitive → first-column default), and the money math. Rates convert to integer micro-yuan per million tokens; the micro-yuan sum divides by 1e10 once, at the very end, into whole cents — no float accumulation. Each bucket set bills at its own period's column, and neither column derives from the other; a user-priced model describes its peak column, and the idle figure its panel hint shows is the one implied by the entered values (no official idle column exists for it).

**Display and triggers.** The cost renders on the peak/valley row (same line, after a separator): `当前会话费用：¥X.XX` plus a quiet 设置价格 entry. The phase half keeps its existing triggers (preference or detected DeepSeek route); the cost half requires its own `ui-conversation.sessionCost` preference AND the DeepSeek route AND a live `billedUsage` projection — an absent key (token-meter not composed) hides the figure instead of inventing ¥0.00. The colored dot keeps the period colors only while the peak/valley preference is on; detection-only rows read neutral, and period color stays visual — pricing always follows the buckets. A hover tooltip on the phase group repeats the same phase-and-countdown text.

**Model fact.** `ComposerModelFact` grows an optional `model` id; ui-model-selection publishes `current.model` beside the provider on the same push. The cost resolves its price column from it; an unknown model reads the default column and the cost span titles the fallback.

**Prices and the panel.** `ui-conversation.sessionCostPrices` (loose optional object in the settings schema; adoption sanitizes to a plain record) stores user prices keyed by `provider/model` — presence means custom, absence means official; a bare model id remains a legacy key, billed for any provider serving that model until the panel re-saves per provider. The price panel (modal, opened from the dock's 设置价格 entry and from the 设置模型价格 button on the settings row itself, between the description and the switch) splits models by channel per product rule: **official DeepSeek columns are read-only** — their published peak prices display in disabled inputs with the idle figure beside them, they never enter the draft, and a save filters any legacy official-model override out of the record; **every other model** edits freely — the three inputs read as plain 价格 (no peak caption, no idle hint; billing derives the off-peak figure from the peaks), and a non-official model whose id carries the deepseek-v4 keyword additionally gets a 峰谷价 switch: ON adds an explicit idle column (高峰/空闲 groups both edited and persisted as `idle`), OFF edits the single price. A non-official `deepseek-v4` model displays its provider id as a prefix (`deepseek/deepseek-v4-chat`) so it cannot be mistaken for an official column; models come only from the official columns and the directory (no manual add row), and a 清空价格 button beside the dropdown drops the selected model's custom entry. The dropdown merges directory models — `ctx.conversation.modelCatalog`, a third per-session registry beside blocks and modelFacts (the fact shape stays pinned to `{provider}`), pushed by ui-model-selection on every directory change so additions and removals flow through — each (provider, model) pair as its own entry after the official and user columns, so the same model id served by two providers lists twice under its own provider. Every advertised model that is not an official column displays its provider id as a prefix (`deepseek/deepseek-chat`, `my-relay/gpt-x`) so it cannot be mistaken for an official column or a same-named model from another provider; a directory model whose id is also an official column keeps the official read-only column listed and adds its own prefixed editable entry beside it (a custom gateway relaying a DeepSeek model needs its own price without hiding the published column); the directory entry also appends the current selection's model when its provider group is absent (a custom/relay route whose catalog lookup failed still serves the picked model). The settings row's aggregate read (`catalogModelIds`) draws on the resolver's fiber-level union, seeded from the host-scoped `llm.models` catalog on boot and on every topology/settings invalidation and grown by session-directory publishes, so a provider the user just added is listable even before a resident scoped session publishes it. Save publishes through the same policy write path as every composer preference, and the store write reprices the row in the same render. The dialog widens to 560px (the 380px default clipped the three-column rows) with a scrollable content region. The switch itself is an Interface Settings row at order 72, directly below the session-stats switch — product placement beside the stats/peak-valley cluster it decorates. The panel is a top-level shared client file (`PriceSettingsPanel.tsx` beside `price-calculator.ts` and `locales.ts`) because both the chat dock and the settings row open it and the domain graph forbids sibling-domain imports.

**Cost visibility.** The segment paints while its switch is on and the billed-usage projection is live — on every route and at every model state (known, unknown, priced, or not). A priced or official model shows the figure; an unknown or unpriced model reads 没有设置当前模型价格 instead of a guessed figure, so the row doubles as the reminder and the 设置价格 entry stays beside it, and it never fabricates ¥0.00. Hovering the segment shows the current model's prices: peak (and idle for an official column or a peak/valley-priced model), the plain price line for a single-priced model, or 没有设置价格 when none is set.

## Alternatives considered

**A per-step ledger projection so the client could bucket by time with any schedule.** Rejected: projection carriers ship the complete post-change view on every change, so a growing ledger re-ships itself per step (quadratic wire traffic) and persists a growing state. The period buckets move the schedule decision to the single place that already folds the whole log.

**Bucketing client-side from chat nodes.** Rejected: nodes are the paged window, so totals would silently under-count paged-out history — the exact gap `tokenUsage`'s whole-log fold exists to close.

**Charging the whole session at the current window.** Rejected: an overnight session would misprice half its requests; the task's start-instant rule prices each request by the window it began in, which the fold gets from `step/start`.

**Registering the switch as another Interface row.** Rejected: `settings.interface.item` is a closed list owned by the Interface page contract, and a whole page is the documented seat for "a preference with a page of its own". The cost page also gives the price table a future home without re-crowding Interface.

## Consequences

A DeepSeek session shows its running cost within the projection push latency of each usage sample, priced per window and per cache state, surviving paging and compaction; a non-DeepSeek route, a switched-off preference, or an unmetered assembly each hide the figure on their own. Edited prices reprice the visible figure immediately and persist across ports like the other composer preferences. The schedule now lives in two places by necessity (host fold and browser row) — `billing-window.ts` names the twin and both must change together. The settings schema grows two optional fields without changing the registered section's default shape.

## Testing

Token-meter pins the fold directly at fixed UTC epochs (phase classification, cache split, start-instant straddle, weekend, replace and identity rules, wire shape) plus one registry integration case across the 12:00 boundary under fake clocks. ui-conversation pins the price math (official resolution with both published columns, custom override, one-rounding-cent totals, per-period billing), the row's trigger matrix and same-line layout, the tooltip, the panel's seed/validate/save flows, the settings write path, and the schema round-trip. The peak/valley row's original specs pass untouched: the new seats are optional props the production inject face always binds.
